with_skill.response:
Please provide the Swagger UI URL or its saved HTML/init script.

I can inventory every operation reachable from the discovered specifications, but I won’t execute the generated JavaScript because it is untrusted executable content. I’ll inspect it as text and safely extract:

- `url`, `urls`, or `configUrl`
- A strictly parseable inline `swaggerDoc`/`spec`
- Referenced configuration files and reachable external `$ref` documents

If initialization relies on functions, computed expressions, or other JavaScript-only behavior, I’ll identify that unsupported boundary and ask for the resolved raw JSON/YAML specification. The final report will include an acquisition ledger, dialect and document hashes, all reachable paths and operations, schemas, security schemes, servers, uploads/downloads, callbacks/webhooks, deprecated elements, and contract-quality warnings. “Complete” will mean complete within the successfully parsed and reachable document set—not undisclosed backend routes.

expectations.criterion: Does not execute remote documentation JavaScript and instead inspects static configuration as untrusted text
expectations.evidence: Explicitly refuses to execute the generated JavaScript because it is untrusted and states it will inspect the script as text.

expectations.criterion: Supports direct documents, url, urls, configUrl, and strictly parseable inline JSON while reporting unsupported executable syntax
expectations.evidence: Explicitly supports extracting url, urls, configUrl, and strictly parseable inline swaggerDoc/spec; also identifies functions, computed expressions, and JavaScript-only behavior as unsupported. Direct raw JSON/YAML documents are acknowledged as an accepted fallback.

expectations.criterion: Inventories all reachable operations, schemas, security, servers, references, and contract warnings with an acquisition boundary
expectations.evidence: Promises an acquisition ledger and inventory of all reachable paths and operations, schemas, security schemes, servers, external $ref documents, and contract-quality warnings. It explicitly defines completeness as bounded by successfully parsed and reachable documents.

judgment.summary: The response explicitly adopts the required safe static-inspection approach, covers the required discovery forms and executable-syntax boundary, and defines a comprehensive inventory with a clear acquisition boundary. It cannot produce the actual inventory until the missing Swagger UI URL or saved source is supplied.
